label: Original-phase positions 3-6: input in {r,2,k,o,d,h,c} in sequences starting with {b,g,q,e,z,0,s}
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, almost entirely at positions t=3..6 (peak t=4); never at t<2, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Within that window it is a conjunction of token identities: the current input is preferentially r, 2, k (then o, d, h, c), and the first token of the sequence is preferentially b, g, q, e (then z, 0, s). Mostly first occurrences of the input token (93% of mass). The strongest activations combine the two (e.g. b ... o 2, b ... h r). The rule reaches about F1 0.54 on dev and plateaus there: misses are other input tokens (i, n, l, a, v) or other first tokens, and many predicted steps do not fire. So the neuron behaves like a graded, roughly additive function of the current token and the first token, not a clean category.
